My initial verdict of INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE was incorrect. Upon reconsideration, the evidence does support the claim that energy generation and storage revenue for FY2025 increased by more than 20% compared to FY2024.

The key insight from weakness #2 is that E1 provides full-year data for the energy generation and storage segment. While E1 explicitly states that COST increased by 20%, it also states that gross margin improved from 26.2% to 29.8%. Using the margin formula: if Cost = Revenue × (1 - Margin), then with a 20% cost increase and margin improving from 26.2% to 29.8%, revenue must have increased by more than 20%. Specifically: Prior year cost/revenue ratio was 73.8% (1-0.262), current year was 70.2% (1-0.298). If costs increased 20%, from the relationship Cost_2025/Cost_2024 = 1.20 and (Revenue_2025 × 0.702)/(Revenue_2024 × 0.738) = 1.20, we get Revenue_2025/Revenue_2024 = 1.20 × (0.738/0.702) = 1.261, or approximately 26% growth.

This is further corroborated by weakness #3: the partial-year data shows H1 2025 growth of 19% and Q3 2025 growth of 44%, indicating accelerating growth throughout the year that would result in full-year growth exceeding 20%.

The claim is SUPPORTED by the evidence.
